title: Taiwan Challenges Beijing's World War Narrative Following Trump-Xi Meeting
seoTitle: Taiwan Counters Beijing Narrative After Trump-Xi Meeting
subtitle: Discussion on Taiwan was highlighted during the latest meeting between the two leaders
excerpt: The Trump-Xi meeting in Washington highlighted Taiwan's stance on China. Taiwan's UN representative noted that the topic was not addressed in depth.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The latest meeting between former President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington brought Taiwan's position toward China to the forefront. Taiwan's representative to the US, Alexander Yui, stated that the topic was not discussed in depth, but remains central to relations between the countries.

The Trump-Xi meeting and the discussion on Taiwan

During Trump's visit to Beijing, the issue of Taiwan was mentioned, but was not the primary focus of the meeting. Yui reported that, although China stated the issue is “fundamental,” there was no reaction from the US, which maintained its unchanged position regarding Taiwan.

US reaction and support for Taiwan

Ahead of the visit, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo met with foreign ministers from Japan and Korea, reinforcing support for the stability of the Taiwan Strait and for Taiwan's significant role in international organizations. Taiwan's representative highlighted that the US continues to be the country's primary arms supplier.

Historical context and misunderstandings

Yui clarified that the narrative that the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) fought in World War II is incorrect. He explained that the CCP only became the People's Republic of China in 1949 and that, during the war, only guerrilla groups existed. This information was used to challenge claims made by Trump during the visit.

Taiwan's needs and military support

Taiwan's representative requested that the US deliver the $14 billion arms package that has not yet been fulfilled. He emphasized the need to strengthen Taiwan's defense and protect the semiconductor industry, which is considered vital to global technology.

Impact on regional security

Yui pointed out that the CCP seeks to drive a wedge between the US and its allies, including Japan and Korea, and that Taiwan needs ongoing support to ensure regional stability and security.

With information from Yahoo, CBS News.
